title: The locks decide your cabin size
subtitle: A river vessel is built to fit the smallest lock on its route. Everything follows.

text: Nothing on a river ship is wider than the lock it must pass.
sub: Length, width and height are set by the infrastructure — locks and low bridges — not by the naval architect. The long, low silhouette is engineering, not styling.

left.label: River
items: A sundeck, not a pool deck

title: What the space is spent on

items.head: The view, not the floor plan
items.body: French balconies and full-height glass take priority. You are meant to be looking out, constantly.

items.head: The sundeck
items.body: The best room on a river ship has no ceiling. It is where the week happens between locks.

items.head: One good dining room
items.body: No specialty booking game. One kitchen, cooking for a hundred-odd people who eat together.

quote: You are not buying square footage on a river. You are buying the window.

text: Compare the cabin to a hotel room and it loses. Compare the week.
sub: You will be ashore or on the sundeck for most of the daylight. The cabin is where you sleep and where you watch the bank go past at breakfast.

title: Send this to the person who'd be sharing it
body: Or tell me the river and the month, and I'll come back with the two cabin grades actually worth the difference.
